channel.title: AI News Radar
channel.description: A curated 24-hour radar of AI news: official releases, new models and high-signal discussion.

item.title: Transformers Model Integration Contracts
item.description: A 66 MB UMT5 fixture lets transformers-mic replay five months of commits on CPU, catching a July 30 to September 28, 2026 regression where enabling PyTorch SDPA let UMT5's decoder attend to future tokens. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: Scaling Git at OpenAI
item.description: OpenAI built Pando, a Git-compatible backend for Codex-scale development across its monorepo, cutting median push latency nearly 5x while transferring close to 1PB of Git data daily. (OpenAI News)

item.title: The latest AI news we announced in October 2026
item.description: Gemini 4 Argon launched globally for developers and enterprises in October 2026, followed two weeks later by Gemini 4 Carbon for long-term engineering and cybersecurity defense, with Google also introducing Genie 4 for real-time interactive simulations. (Google AI Blog)

item.title: Security risk assessments include repository protection status
item.description: Security risk assessments include repository protection status (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: Rewarding defenders with bigger bug bounties
item.description: OpenAI has raised median Security Bug Bounty payouts for medium, high and critical vulnerabilities more than fourfold, with critical flaws in core products like ChatGPT now topping $30,000 and quality, loyalty and priority campaign bonuses pushing exceptional finds to $172,000. (OpenAI News)

item.title: pull_request_target blocked by default December 2
item.description: GitHub Actions will block pull_request_target events by default in all public repositories from December 2, 2026, unless an Actions event policy explicitly allows them, after a delay from November 2, with Insights available until November 9 to identify affected workflows. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: Run 128K ultra-long context on just 8GB of VRAM! Open-source local LLM tool Strata 0.2.10 released
item.description: Strata 0.2.10 dynamically adjusts VRAM and RAM allocation so 8GB-VRAM devices can run Qwen3.8IQ3_S at a 128K (131,072-token) context, with official DFlash2-mode tests generating 63–73 tokens/s. (AIbase)

item.title: Preparing our next security sprint to harden OpenAI
item.description: OpenAI is planning its next internal security sprint with Cathedral Systems to stress-test defenses using its own models, with rewards for key findings raised more than fourfold after 25% of product engineers used Codex to reproduce vulnerabilities and prepare patches. (OpenAI News)

item.title: App Store's new age-rating rules take effect next month, officially relegating AI virtual lovers to Apple's adult category
item.description: Apple's App Store age-rating overhaul, announced November 3, requires developers from November 16 to declare location-sharing, dating and AI companion features, with virtual partners pushed into the 18+ tier and all apps compliant by January 12, 2027. (AIbase)

item.title: Introducing the Grid Protectors Program
item.description: OpenAI's Grid Protectors Program pairs future compute campuses with utilities to cut power use when the grid is strained, including a Georgia Power agreement for up to 1,000 MW of flexible demand response, aiming to protect consumer electricity costs. (OpenAI News)

item.title: Kimi no longer just writes design docs: it now jumps straight into Unity and Unreal projects to build game prototypes
item.description: Moonshot AI's November 2 game development and creative work solution, built on Kimi K3.1, connects to Unity, Unreal Engine and Blender so Kimi can operate editors, rewrite existing projects and deliver editable files plus operation logs. (AIbase)

item.title: LifeVal
item.description: LifeVal, OpenAI's new benchmark, tests whether AI can help with everyday tasks like finding childcare, managing finances and government paperwork, drawing on a 3,995-person survey and two time-use studies for over 1 billion weekly ChatGPT users. (OpenAI News)

item.title: QuestMobile: Doubao and DeepSeek top other AI apps in monthly uses per user
item.description: QuestMobile’s Nov. 3 China Mobile Internet Autumn Report shows Doubao and DeepSeek led September AI app usage at 72.0 and 65.9 monthly uses per user, with DeepSeek up 5.8% month over month as competition shifts to high-frequency engagement. (AIbase)

item.title: SenseTime officially launches SenseNova 6.8 Flash, focused on real-world task execution and design collaboration
item.description: SenseTime released the official version of SenseNova 6.8 Flash on November 3, adding long-term memory and cross-session collaboration plus dynamic PPT, Agentic 3D design and deep Figma integration for real task execution. (AIbase)

item.title: Compute costs too steep to bear? SpaceX reportedly quietly cuts Grok Bot quotas as Musk admits revenue and spending are out of balance
item.description: SpaceX reportedly halved Grok Bot usage quotas as Musk acknowledged on X that running costs are unsustainable against revenue, after Gwynne Shotwell said in early October weekly paid users reached 80,000, more than double month-over-month. (AIbase)

item.title: Linkly AI Clipper — Save web as an Agent-friendly Markdown browser extension
item.description: Linkly AI Clipper is a browser extension that saves web pages as Agent-friendly Markdown, aiming to make web content easier for AI agents to read and use. (Product Hunt)

item.title: Apple’s ‘Ultra’ smart home robot might have to wait until 2028
item.description: Apple's rumored J595 desktop robot, possibly named HomeView Ultra, has had hardware finished for about two years while software lags, pushing its launch to 2028 with a 9-inch swiveling screen, FaceTime tracking and a possible price above $1,000. (The Verge)

item.title: Alibaba has open-sourced 470 Qwen models, and Joseph Tsai says open source is the key to bringing AI to everyone.
item.description: At the 2026 World Internet Conference in Wuzhen, Alibaba chairman Joseph Tsai said Qwen has open-sourced over 470 models with more than 4 billion cumulative global downloads and over 330,000 derivative models, arguing that open source is the key to making AI widely accessible. (AIbase)

item.title: Cedric AI for Meetings — The first AI agent to present your slides and attend for you
item.description: Cedric AI for Meetings is billed as the first AI agent that presents your slides and attends meetings on your behalf, though a CAPTCHA gate left the page's claimed details unverified. (Product Hunt)
